supplemental_static_sink_audit.effect: Diagnostic prioritization only; does not resolve or dismiss CodeQL alerts.

blockers: Eight medium-severity CodeQL alerts are reported in code changed by PR #62 and have not yet been individually triaged or resolved.

The supplemental static sink audit found 52 review/diagnostic sink observations across 151 Python files; none were classified high_review, but 50 CLI-derived filesystem sinks and 2 dynamic network calls still require correlation against the actual CodeQL dataflows before disposition.
next_actions: Map each CodeQL alert to file, line, rule and dataflow before remediation or false-positive disposition.
Correlate the eight CodeQL alerts against the 50 CLI-derived filesystem sink observations and 2 dynamic network calls; do not infer equivalence without matching file/line/dataflow evidence.
Patch true positives with path confinement, allowlisting, least privilege, explicit network allowlists or other sink-specific fail-closed controls and add negative tests.
Document any false-positive disposition with rule, source, sink, reason, reproducer/negative test and reviewer evidence.
Re-run CodeQL and require zero unresolved medium/high/critical alerts before merge.
claims_boundary: A successful CodeQL check run or static sink audit does not mean zero vulnerabilities. CodeQL explicitly reports eight new medium-severity alerts in changed code. The supplemental audit is diagnostic only and cannot dismiss those alerts; this gate therefore remains merge_allowed=false until each alert is resolved or independently justified as a false positive under the recorded policy.
